chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performs the ritual bath (ghusl) for entering Mecca, then sleeps and performs ablution (wudu) before entering; does that suffice for him or must he repeat it? He said, 'It does not suffice for him, because he entered with only ablation.'
ai.seo_question: Does sleeping invalidate the ritual bath (ghusl) for entering Mecca, requiring a new ablution (wudu)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the entry into the Masjid al-Haram requires an active state of minor ablution (wudu), rendering the initial major bath (ghusl) insufficient if wudu is lost or not maintained. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of ritual purity for specific acts of worship, distinguishing between the preparatory ghusl and the requisite wudu for the actual entry. The hadith highlights the precision in fiqh regarding the conditions of validity for entering the sacred precincts.
